newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Taiwan's Huan Hsin seeks Singapore listing -paper.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's Huan Hsin seeks Singapore listing -paper.

text.p: Taiwan's telephone cord and accessories group Huan Hsin Holdings is seeking a listing on the main board of the Stock Exchange of Singapore (SES), the Straits Times newspaper said on Wednesday.
It said the group had submitted its application to the SES and the initial public offering (IPO), expected to be denominated in US dollars, would be lead managed by OCBC Bank.
Part of the IPO's proceeds will be used to fund Huan Hsin's business expanion.
"We will invest US$15 million in a new plant in Shanghai," Huan Hsin's director and general manager Hsu Cheng Chien was quoted as saying.
Besides making power cords, he said the new plant would have plastic injection moulding facilities to make accessories such as telephone handsets, TV monitor casings and calculator casings.

The group would look into producing plastic products for industries other than telecommunications, computer and consumer electronics industries, Hsu Hung Chun, the group's president was quoted as saying.
Construction of the plant has started and will be completed by the end of July.
Huan Hsin supplies to original equipment manufacturers, accounting for 60 percent of supplies to branded telephone producers, the company said.
Sales of telephone cords now account for 75 percent of group turnover.
Huan Hsin recorded a pretax profit of US$7.2 million on a turnover of US$33.8 million in 1996.
It has a factory in Shanghai and one in Malaysia. It intends to close its plant in Taiwan and move production to Shanghai, the ST said.
